# Multi-Agent System Observability

Observability for systems that orchestrate multiple AI agents via
LangGraph within Temporal workflows. What's different, what tools exist,
and how to instrument the Temporal→LangGraph boundary.

## Key Finding

OpenTelemetry is converging as the standard for agent observability,
with GenAI semantic conventions (Development status) already adopted by
Datadog, Langfuse, OpenLLMetry, and Arize Phoenix. However, multi-agent
conventions (task hierarchies, team coordination) are still in proposal
stage. The practical gap: cost and quality metrics have no OTEL standard
— they remain application-level concerns.

## Quick Decision Framework

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Which tracing platform?** | Langfuse (self-hosted, MIT, OTEL-native) or OpenLLMetry + any OTEL backend for vendor neutrality |
| **How do Temporal and LangGraph traces connect?** | Both emit OTEL spans via TracingInterceptor and OpenLLMetry — spans auto-nest via Python contextvars when running in the same process |
| **What OTEL conventions to use?** | Adopt gen_ai.* now (Development status), opt in via OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental |
| **First alerts to set up?** | Tool error rate spikes + cost-per-workflow anomalies catch the most failures with minimal setup |
| **How to track costs?** | gen_ai.client.token.usage metric + Langfuse Metrics API for aggregated cost queries |
